Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
227 PM EDT Thu Aug 20 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 226 PM EDT Thursday...

Trends continue to depict a dry slot between a pair of systems 
Saturday and Sunday for Vermont.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 226 PM EDT Thursday...

1. Dry and seasonable conditions are expected as we head into 
the weekend on Friday and Saturday. 

2. A pair of systems will increase precipitation chances across 
northern New York and southeastern Vermont into the latter portion 
of the weekend.

3. Quiescent conditions next week

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 226 PM EDT Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Dry and relatively seasonable conditions are expected to 
prevail through the end of the week with high pressure nudging into 
the region from the northwest. Ahead of the area of high pressure 
widespread mid to high clouds will remain over the area until 
tonight as dry air aloft helps to scour our mid to upper level 
moisture. Some light shower activity currently over southern New 
York may briefly kiss southern Rutland and Windsor Counties late 
this afternoon/evening (rain chances less than 20%), though with 
dewpoint depressions between 20-30 degrees, any radar returns will 
likely fall as virga or just light sprinkles. Clouds will clear this 
evening for most of the region, outside of perhaps southeastern 
Vermont, with some lingering low level moisture. Decoupling, similar 
to last night, will lead to patchy valley fog in the favored 
locations. Locations near Lake Champlain may also see a lake cloud 
reduce visibilities due to the temperature difference between the 
cooling air and the warmer Lake Champlain. Temperatures overnight 
tonight will fall into the upper 40s to low 50s for most areas; mid 
50s for the Champlain Valley. Fog will scour out after sunrise 
tomorrow morning with a pleasant day on Friday. Temperatures will 
warm into the mid to upper 70s to near 80 tomorrow with mostly clear 
skies. Light northerly channeled flow in the Champlain Valley may 
create some light breezes, but by and large calm and variable winds 
will be the theme across the area tomorrow. Clouds begin to increase 
across southeastern Vermont late Friday into Saturday as a weak 
coastal low in southern New England tracks up the coast. 
Temperatures Friday night will be cooler across the northern and 
western cloud free locations falling into the upper 40s to low 50s; 
mid 50s for the Champlain Valley and southern Vermont. Shower 
activity will increase as the coastal system and an approaching 
Great Lakes trough move about New England through the weekend.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Following a calm start to the weekend, conditions will 
turn more wet and showery by the latter portion of the weekend. As 
high pressure drifts to the northwest, it will leave in its wake an 
area of subsidence and subtle ridging centered from northeast to 
southwest across Vermont Saturday and Sunday. A pair of systems will 
split this area of ridging bringing shower chances to portions of 
the area. The first of the two systems will be a weak coastal low 
along the coast of southern New England, which will track near Cape 
Cod and is expected to continue moving northeast out into the Gulf 
of Maine. Some showers may be possible in eastern Windsor and Orange 
Counties Saturday afternoon and evening, however, recent trends have 
suggested precipitation associated with the coastal system will stay 
east of the Connecticut River. Any showers that do develop in 
southeastern Vermont will be light in nature. 

The second, higher confidence, system will be an approaching long 
wave trough that will track east from the Great Lakes region. The 
trough translates east into the St. Lawrence Valley late Saturday 
into early Sunday, with scattered rounds of showers. The trough 
slowly tracks east through the day Sunday reaching Vermont by late 
Sunday into Sunday night. While an isolated rumble of thunder with 
the shower activity cannot be ruled out, chances are decreasing with 
poor mid level lapse rates, cool surface temperatures, and a lack of 
true instability. In all likelihood, the boundary will be a mess of 
scattered to isolated showers with some breaks in between, focused 
mainly over northern New York, and somewhat weakening as it moves 
east. Between both systems during the day Saturday, and most of 
Sunday, Vermont will be straddled between in a "no mans land" of dry 
and cloudy conditions. Chances for showers do not increase for 
Vermont until Sunday afternoon, though some isolated sprinkles or 
mist, especially in the higher terrain, due to low to mid level 
stratus clouds. Precipitation amounts will be light, especially 
across Vermont, with probabilities of half an inch in the 25th to 
75th percentiles, and probabilities of an inch or more below 25%. 
The higher amounts around a quarter to half an inch will be in 
northern New York, primarily in the northern St. Lawrence Valley. 
Lower amount expected in central and northern Vermont. The trough 
will pull away to the northeast heading towards Monday.

KEY MESSAGE 3: The extended forecast begins with the precipitation 
associated with Sunday's trough moving east of the region and a surface 
high pressure moving in behind. The high pressure will dominate for 
most of the rest of the week. Daytime highs will gradually increase 
from the mid 70s into the upper 70s throughout the week. By late week, 
the flow turns more zonal and could allow for precipitation to return. 
A couple weak systems appear will try to make their way into our CWA 
Thursday and Friday, but impactful weather is not anticipated at this 
time.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z THURSDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Through 18Z Friday...VFR conditions will prevail today, with winds
remaining under 10kt. Some high clouds are streaming in, developing
into a BKN200 deck by this afternoon. Overnight, calm winds will
allow fog development in the climatologically preferred areas. SLK
and MPV are the surest bet for IFR conditions overnight with EFK a
little less certain. MSS could go down as well, but for now showing
vis reducing into MVFR criteria.

Outlook...

Friday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Saturday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Slight
chance SHRA.
Sunday: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Likely SHRA, Slight
chance TSRA.
Sunday Night: MVFR/IFR conditions possible. Slight chance SHRA,
Slight chance TSRA.
Monday: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. Chance SHRA, Slight
chance TSRA.
Monday Night: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Tuesday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.

&&
